summary: King County, WA L-5 cab lookout on the Cascade crest, built 1935 and removed or destroyed in 1965; a 2022 hike write-up reports rusted metal remains on the summit.

facts.design: L-5 cab (Willhite: 'said to be' an L-5 cab); no tower height is given in the sources
facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1965 (register) or destroyed that year (Firelookout.com, Willhite); a 2022 hike write-up reports rusted metal remains on the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest per the register (Washington Lookouts says Snoqualmie National Forest)

visit.trail_note: Willhite's simplest route starts at Stampede Pass, reached from I-90 at exit 62, with high clearance recommended. The route includes a short bushwhack with brushy game trails

events.note: Osborne photo team panoramas show cut trees and a line that may be phone or clothes line (Willhite)
First structure, said to be an L-5 cab (Willhite); register and Firelookout.com both give 1935
Cab removed (register) or destroyed (Firelookout.com, Willhite) in 1965; Washington Lookouts lists it as Removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says removed in 1965; Firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1965. All agree on the year.
Register names Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest; Washington Lookouts names Snoqualmie National Forest. The story uses the register's name.

sources.title: Snowshoe Butte by Crossover Butte via Stampede Pass

notes_for_editor: Brief kind 'ground' matches the Forest Fire Lookout Association list (type Ground), so no correction. Sources describe only an L-5 cab, so the tower question stays open. No staffing or fire history appears in the sources read, so none is given. Access level is left out because no source states whether the road or summit is public. Remains rest on a 2022 blog and Willhite's captions.
